pricing.title: Free during beta.
pricing.foot: No card needed. Your own provider keys don't count. A self-hosted instance sets its own limits.

limits.label: Free beta limits
limits.fetches: MCP fetches an hour, per token
limits.callsDetail: A call is one transcript, with or without a recording. Deleting a call frees its place.
limits.minutesDetail: Counted by audio length. Transcripts you upload ready-made don't count.
limits.storageDetail: Encrypted and compressed on your device. With your own bucket, there is no limit from us.
limits.asksDetail: One question about one call. Resets at midnight UTC.
limits.tokensDetail: For the local agent, remote MCP and scripts. Each token has its own scopes.
limits.fetchesDetail: Ciphertext fetches over remote MCP. The local agent decrypts on your machine.

legal.a: It depends on where you and the other person are. Many places allow recording a call you take part in; some require everyone on the call to agree. Check the rules where you work. AskCalls doesn't record calls; it stores what you upload.

lost.q: What if I lose my phone?
lost.a: Unlock on another device with your passkey, if it syncs, or with your recovery code. If you lose every passkey and the recovery code, your calls can't be recovered: we never had your keys.

staff.q: Can AskCalls staff see my calls?
staff.a: No. We store ciphertext and keyed tokens. Without your keys, which never reach us, there is nothing to read.

where.a: On askcalls.com, in Frankfurt: Postgres on Neon and storage on Cloudflare R2 in its EU jurisdiction, encrypted on your device before upload. Recording backups can go to your own bucket instead.

selfHost.a: Yes. Run docker compose up and a setup wizard walks you through the database, storage, sign-in and providers.

hebrew.a: Yes. The interface, search and transcription work in Hebrew and English, mixed in one call. Search handles Hebrew prefixes, so “בחולון” finds “חולון”.

providers.q: Which AI and transcription providers can I use?
providers.a: Transcription: ElevenLabs Scribe v2 by default, or OpenAI, Deepgram, Soniox or any OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint. Questions: Anthropic by default, or OpenAI, Google or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama and LM Studio included. You can switch each to your own key or turn it off.

remote.q: What does the remote MCP endpoint see?
remote.a: It has no keys, so it offers only inbox uploads, recent call ids with their days and durations, and your account status. Inbox uploads are visible to the server in transit, then encrypted to your inbox key.

delete.q: How do I delete my account?
delete.a: In Settings. Deleting the account deletes the wrapped keys, so the remaining ciphertext can never be decrypted, and then deletes the data. Export first if you want a decrypted copy; the export is decrypted on your device.

open.a: Yes, under the MIT licence. Every release publishes the SHA-256 of each client JavaScript asset, so you can check that askcalls.com serves the code in the repository.

limit.a: Uploads pause until you delete calls or the month resets. Search, reading, playback and export keep working, and nothing is deleted.

ownKeys.a: Transcription and questions with your own key don't count toward the limits. The key is encrypted with your keys and used only on your device.

selfHostFree.a: Yes. The code is MIT-licensed. You pay only for the server, storage and providers you choose, or nothing if it all runs locally.

securityPage.lead: This is the whole privacy model: what we store, what we never see, where plaintext goes when you ask, and how to check all of it yourself.

stores.title: What we store, and what we never see.
stores.body: Your device indexes and encrypts before anything leaves it. The server receives ciphertext and tokens, and returns them when you search.
stores.yes1: Encrypted transcripts, metadata, notes and recordings
stores.yes2: HMAC tokens for keywords, contacts and tags
stores.yes4: The day of each call and a duration bucket
stores.no3: Tag names, notes or rule definitions

plaintext.title: Where plaintext goes.
plaintext.body: Only when you ask, one request at a time. These routes stream straight through and never write to disk, storage or logs.
plaintext.transcriptionBody: Audio of a call you upload. Where the provider issues single-use tokens, your browser sends the audio to it directly and our server never sees it; otherwise it streams through our server. With your own key, your device always sends it directly.
plaintext.askBody: That one call and your question, after you agree in a dialog that names the receiver. The transcript is wrapped as untrusted data, so instructions inside it aren't followed.
plaintext.inboxBody: A transcript a remote AI tool sends for you is visible to our server in transit, sealed at once to your inbox public key, and the plaintext is discarded. The app says so next to each such item.
plaintext.retentionBody: The terms each adapter works under, as documented in its README in the repository.
plaintext.elevenlabs: Requests carry enable_logging=false, which ElevenLabs honours only for workspaces with Zero Retention Mode, an Enterprise feature. Until that is in place, ElevenLabs may keep request logs under its standard policy.
plaintext.deepgram: Requests carry mip_opt_out=true, opting out of Deepgram's Model Improvement Program; Deepgram then keeps the data only as long as needed to process the request.
plaintext.openaiStt: No per-request retention flag. API inputs aren't used for training by default; zero data retention is an account-level agreement with OpenAI.
plaintext.soniox: No no-retention flag. The adapter deletes the uploaded file and the transcription as soon as it has the transcript; Soniox's 30-day expiry is the backstop.
plaintext.anthropic: No per-request retention flag; retention follows the instance's agreement with Anthropic.
plaintext.openaiLlm: Requests send store: false, so the Responses API doesn't store them.
plaintext.local: Ollama, LM Studio or a local Whisper server: requests stay on the network you run them on.

keys.title: Your keys.
keys.body: One root key is created on your first device and never leaves a device unwrapped. Every other key comes from it.
keys.label: Key hierarchy
keys.rootDetail: 32 random bytes · wiped from memory on lock

unlock.title: Unlocking.
unlock.body: Each method keeps its own wrapped copy of the root key. Sign-up can't finish until you create a recovery code and type part of it back.
unlock.passkey: Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key. The PRF extension yields 32 bytes the server never sees.
unlock.recovery: 8 groups of 4 characters, shown once. 128 bits of randomness, so no slow derivation is needed.
unlock.passphrase: Only where the browser lacks PRF. Argon2id at 64 MiB, at least 12 characters.
unlock.lockingBody: After 15 idle minutes and on tab close. Keys and decrypted text are dropped from memory.

link.title: Linking a device.
link.body: The local agent or another browser receives the root key straight from your existing device, encrypted to a key made for it. The server only relays.
link.step1: In Settings › Devices, choose Link a device to get a short code and a QR code.
link.step2: The new device makes a key pair and posts its public key.
link.step3: Both devices show a 6-digit fingerprint. You confirm they match.
link.step4: The trusted device sends the root key encrypted to the new public key.
link.step5: The link expires in 10 minutes, is written to the audit log and can be revoked.

verify.title: Verify what you run.
verify.body: AskCalls builds reproducibly. Every release publishes the SHA-256 of each client JavaScript asset, so you can check that askcalls.com serves exactly the code in the repository. App routes load no third-party scripts and run under a strict CSP.

leak.title: The leak test.
leak.zero: seeded words and phone numbers found in a full dump of the database and the storage bucket.
leak.body: Every pull request runs it: seed calls with known words and numbers, dump the entire database and bucket, and search for them in UTF-8, UTF-16 and every normalized and token form. If anything turns up, the build fails.

report.title: Threat model and reporting.
report.body: AskCalls protects your calls from the server and anyone who gets at it. It can't protect what an unlocked device shows: a compromised device that is unlocked can read it. Report a vulnerability privately through the repository's security advisories, not in a public issue.

faqPage.lead: About recording, keys, where data lives, providers and limits. The security page covers the privacy model in full.

mcpPage.title: Connect your AI.
mcpPage.lead: The askcalls agent is a local MCP server that holds your keys. It searches, decrypts and ingests on your machine, so Claude, Cursor or any MCP client can work with your calls.

link.title: Link the agent.
link.body: Sign in, then link this computer from a device that is already unlocked. Both show the same 6-digit fingerprint before the key moves.

clients.title: Add it to your client.
clients.claudeDesktop: Open Settings → Developer → Edit Config, or edit the file directly. Restart Claude Desktop after saving.
clients.cursor: ~/.cursor/mcp.json for all projects, or .cursor/mcp.json for one.
clients.path: Desktop apps don't always inherit your shell's PATH. If a client can't start the server, replace bunx with its full path from which bunx.

tools.title: Tools.
tools.body: Transcripts are returned as untrusted content in a delimited field, never as instructions.
tools.search: Keyword, contact, tag, intent, date and semantic search, with decrypted results
tools.get: Full transcript and metadata, within a per-session decrypt budget
tools.ingest: Import a single call or a whole folder

ingest.title: Bulk import.
ingest.body: Bulk import from the command line uses the same pipeline as the app.

remote.title: Remote MCP.
remote.body: A remote MCP endpoint serves clients that can't run a local process. It has no keys, so it offers only inbox_upload, list_recent_calls (ids, days and durations) and account_status. Inbox uploads are visible to the server in transit, encrypted to your inbox public key on arrival, and indexed the next time one of your devices unlocks.

selfHostPage.title: Self-host.
selfHostPage.lead: Run the whole product on your own server. The code is MIT-licensed, and your instance sets its own limits, providers and storage.

compose.title: Docker Compose.
compose.body: This brings up Postgres with pgvector, MinIO and the web app. Open the app, and the first-run wizard walks you through the database, storage, sign-in, transcription and LLM. The first user to sign in becomes the admin.

configure.title: Configure.
configure.body: Every setting is editable at /admin/instance. Any environment variable you set locks its setting. .env.example in the repository lists them all.
configure.stepDb: Database: Postgres with pgvector from any provider.
configure.stepBlob: Storage: any S3-compatible bucket or the local file system.
configure.stepAuth: Sign-in: Google, GitHub, email links or local accounts.
configure.stepProviders: Transcription and questions: a managed provider, an OpenAI-compatible server on your network, or off.

offline.title: Offline.
offline.body: With OFFLINE_MODE=true, the instance serves the embedding model, ffmpeg and fonts itself, and the browser calls no provider directly. Point transcription and questions at a local Whisper server and Ollama to keep every request on your network.
offline.planned: Planned: a Compose file for air-gapped installs that adds the local Whisper server and Ollama.

local.title: On one computer.
local.body: askcalls local runs the whole product on your machine, with no server, no Docker and no account: an embedded Postgres, local file storage, and the app bound to 127.0.0.1. Your data stays encrypted on disk, and you still unlock it with a passkey, recovery code or passphrase.
local.planned: Not available in this version: the command is registered in the CLI and lands with local mode.

privacy.title: Privacy policy.
privacy.lead: How askcalls.com handles personal data. The service is built so that we can't read your calls; this policy covers what we can see.
privacy.s1: AskCalls is operated by the entity named here once it is chosen. For your call content, we act as a processor on your behalf; for your account data, we are the controller.
privacy.s2: Your email address and sign-in provider, account settings, usage counts for the limits, and an audit log of reads and writes to your account (ids, times and event types). Your calls, contacts, tags and notes reach us only as ciphertext and keyed tokens we can't reverse.
privacy.s3: Transcript text, words, phone numbers, contact names, tag names, notes, decrypted recordings and your unwrapped keys. Encryption happens on your device before upload.
privacy.s4: Only when you ask: audio you choose to transcribe goes to the transcription provider, and one call goes to the AI provider when you ask about it. These requests stream through and are not stored by us. The subprocessors page lists who receives what.
privacy.s5: The marketing pages may count page views without cookies or personal data. Signing in sets a session cookie, and the language you choose is kept in a cookie. Product analytics in the app are off unless you turn them on in Settings → Privacy.
privacy.s6: Your data stays until you delete it or a retention rule you set removes it. Deleting your account deletes the wrapped keys first, which makes any remaining ciphertext unreadable, then the data.
privacy.s7: You can access, export, correct and delete your data from Settings. The export is decrypted on your device.

terms.title: Terms.
terms.lead: The agreement between you and the operator of askcalls.com for using the hosted service.
terms.s1: AskCalls stores and indexes call transcripts and recordings you upload, encrypted on your device, and lets you search them and ask an AI about them. The software is open source under the MIT licence; these terms cover the hosted service only.
terms.s2: You are responsible for your passkeys, recovery code and passphrase. We never hold your keys, so we can't recover your calls if you lose every unlock method.
terms.s3: You keep all rights to what you upload. You confirm you are allowed to record and store the calls you upload under the laws that apply to you and to the other people on them.
terms.s4: The service is free during beta, within the published limits. Features and limits may change; we will say so on the pricing page before a change takes effect.
terms.s5: Don't use AskCalls to break the law, to store content you have no right to, or to attack the service or other users.
terms.s6: The service is provided as is during beta. Liability terms are set out here once reviewed by counsel.
terms.s7: You can delete your account at any time from Settings. We may suspend accounts that break these terms, after notice where the law allows.

dpa.title: Data processing agreement.
dpa.lead: For customers who process other people's personal data, such as callers, through askcalls.com.
dpa.s1: You are the controller of the call content you upload. The operator of askcalls.com processes it on your instructions as your processor.
dpa.s2: Storage of ciphertext and keyed tokens, search over them, and on your request, streaming of audio to a transcription provider and of one call to an AI provider.
dpa.s3: Encryption on your device with AES-256-GCM under keys we never hold, keyed HMAC tokens for search, a strict content security policy on app routes, audit logging of reads and writes, and a leak test on every change.
dpa.s4: The subprocessors page lists every subprocessor, what it receives and where. We will update it before adding one.
dpa.s5: Data is stored in the EU (Frankfurt). Transcription and AI requests go to the providers listed, which may process them outside the EU.
dpa.s6: You can export your data at any time, decrypted on your device, and delete it. Account deletion removes the wrapped keys first, then the data.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors.
subprocessors.lead: The companies askcalls.com uses to run the service. A self-hosted instance uses only the services its admin configures.
subprocessors.name: Subprocessor
subprocessors.vercel: Hosting of the web app and API
subprocessors.vercelData: Requests to the app: ciphertext, tokens, and the audio and call you send for transcription or questions, in transit
subprocessors.neonData: Ciphertext, keyed tokens, embeddings of redacted text, account data
subprocessors.elevenlabsData: Audio of calls you choose to transcribe, per request
subprocessors.anthropicData: One call's transcript and your question, per request, after you agree
subprocessors.note: With your own provider key, your device calls the provider directly under your own account, and that provider is not our subprocessor.
